📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes labelled Ryan Naderi “a substantial horse” and a textbook example of how to lead the line as a centre-forward after helping Rangers secure a hard-fought 2-1 Premiership victory over Motherwell.

The German striker has been growing in confidence in recent weeks and once again demonstrated his importance to the Ibrox side, combining tireless pressing and intelligent movement which resulted in a scrappy late 88th-minute winner at Fir park.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

McInnes believes Naderi's contribution extends far beyond his goals, insisting his work rate should not overshadow the quality of his all-round performances.

According to recent reports, “Ryan’s game is really strong at the minute. He looks like a very confident boy and so he should be,” McInnes noted. “Wrongly now, when you think of Ryan or people ask me, it’s about him knocking his pan in. His pressing is unbelievable and he’s a massive horse up there. He runs and works and puts people under pressure.

“He looks tired but his performances are always strong. But he gets goals and has an influence. In that system tonight, his was the most vital position for us, in terms of running channels and getting hold of the ball. His touch was one of a really confident player and he led the line brilliantly. It was a proper number nine performance.”.

On his side’s performance, McInnes added: “We got our just rewards in the game, absolutely. I thought it was a very good, strong performance and I’ve been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot tonight. I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week.

“It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance. We mixed the game up well. Our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.”.

Deflated Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson admitted his side struggled to cope with Rangers' early intensity, but felt the early loss of Ibrahim Said to injury was a major blow before his side ran out of energy in the closing stages.

Recent findings suggest that “They are title challengers and we have a really tough start to the game,” he said. “They put us down. When we win it back, we give it away again. They get momentum. I don't think it's a free kick that they get before their first goal, but we should defend much, much better on that defensive corner kick.

Industry observers note that “In that moment, in the same period, we lose Ibrahim [Said], which is really tough for us, given that the players we have on the bench, many of them in the offensive positions, are not ready to play more than 30 to 45 minutes with high intensity. So it was tough to lose him, and therefore, it's strong of the players to come back and score a goal from a set play and equalise.

“But the last 15-20 minutes, Rangers take completely over and we don't have energy enough in that moment to keep the intensity up.”.

Premier League clubs vote 18-2 in favour of footing legal bill for top-flight chiefs if Man City's sponsors sue them for defamation... with City and Nottingham Forest voting against

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.
  • Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.

Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.

Daily Mail Sport understands there was widespread support from clubs to insulate Premier League chief executive Richard Masters and the four other league directors.

The vote passed with 18 clubs in favour, and City and Nottingham Forest against.

It is understood Forest opted to vote that way as they felt they had not been given sufficient information or enough time to consider the proposal and its implications, as opposed to representing a show of support for City.

The matter was the first item on the agenda at the Premier League shareholders' meeting in the Savoy Hotel on Thursday and was addressed swiftly with limited discussion.

Clubs had a paper for the proposed rule change before the meeting and there was significant support to extend the legal protection to individuals on the league's board.

This marks the first time since the Premier League’s inception that insurance arrangements for its board members have been reviewed.

Premier League clubs will foot the bill if Manchester City's sponsors sue for defamation.

In September, City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules after a seven-year legal process.

An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City inflated their revenues by £900million – disguising money from their Abu Dhabi ownership group as sponsorship revenue.

Etihad Airways, owned by the Abu Dhabi government, denied being ‘involved in improper commercial arrangements’ and said it was considering legal action in response to the verdict.

Meanwhile, another City sponsor, Etisalat - a telecommunications company - is also weighing up legal action.

City, though, maintain their innocence and are appealing the decision, which could see them relegated from the top flight.

Scotland’s Scott McTominay capped off a significant week by netting the winner in a Serie A showdown with Torino on Saturday.

The goalscoring midfielder journeyed back to his club side after a mixed November for the national team that included Nations League victory over North Macedonia before defeat against Switzerland. There was exciting news at home with the public announcement he is due to become a father, declared on social media before Saturday’s home encounter against a squad that features Scotland teammates Che Adams and Nathan Patterson.

According to recent reports, mcTominay scored the game’s only goal in a 1-0 win for Napoli, picking up the ball on the edge of the Torino box, before a piledriver that flew into the bottom corner. It comes as more rumours suggest his stunning stint in Naples could be heading for a close, possibly through a major transfer to AC Milan or Real Madrid, or returning to Manchester United.

Recent findings suggest that speaking after his latest moment of importance in light blue, McTominay smiled: "I am feeling much better. It's an important goal, but more importantly we won, we had to win. I'm happy for the fans, we need to get a bit of momentum going, keep winning. In football it's about the next game, and the next game, you have to do your best. We have a team that wants to work, wants to push, and we want to win more games.".

Manchester United sold the 29-year-old who turns 30 next month to the Serie A side in 2024 and that is the only other senior club side he has represented. McTominay’s ties with Adidas are mentioned to have their part in AC Milan keeping an eye on the Scotland star, according to Italian claims, as the Italian giants are left ‘waiting’ alongside Manchester United and La Liga’s Real Madrid.

Contract talks between Napoli and one of their key players are presently on hold for ‘financial reasons.’ Speaking after McTominay’s goal sealed a much-needed three points for his side, boss Massimiliano Allegri mentioned: “The mood wasn’t right because we had so many chances, I told them at half-time to try smiling and we might get a goal.

“They did really well to win this game, while suffering against a strong opponent. Perhaps it is positive that we won under pressure, but we also should’ve done better controlling the tempo, moving the ball from one side to the other. The lads did very well in defending on set plays and corner kicks.

“I just told McTominay not to be already in the position right behind Rasmus Hojlund, but to run into that space, as it would make him harder to mark. If he is already there and not mobile, then obviously he’s going to be easier to control, but he started to move between the lines and did better.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.
  • Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:10.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a new Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk noted.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone claims that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the newly introduced year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.".

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he has had to settle for seven wins in his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Sources indicate that carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Sources indicate that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

Sources indicate that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager noted. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

Industry observers note that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Industry observers note that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Sources indicate that it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

It has been revealed that speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick mentioned: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

Recent findings suggest that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

Recent findings suggest that “We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

Industry observers note that “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

With just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done. Let’s take a look at how the internationals fared.

Whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello. Even those who didn’t head away are only just really returning, with Ruben Amorim offering the squad a week off.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about….

Christian Pulisic probably leaves the break as the star of the week(s). His brace against Haiti helped secure a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, and he then rounded it off with a bicycle kick in the second leg.

After missing the penultimate international break of the season – to ensure he was fully back to fitness – he’s quickly reminded everyone of how key he can be for club and country, scoring his seventh goal of the season in only 13 games.

He’s on fire and there are no signs of him slowing down anytime soon.

You’d then have to speak about Diego Moreira, who has left the international break – somehow – with more praise than he started it with. He starred in Belgium’s 2-1 win against Turkiye and then followed that up with a goal against Italy.

It gets to a point where you run out of superlatives to describe a player and his teammates are already at that stage. Both Mark Van Bommel and Koni De Winter have called him crazy (in a good way), with the former even putting him in the same group as Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

He’s become a starter for the Red Devils and it’s difficult to see that changing.

According to recent reports, in terms of the Italians, Milan had a few reasons to smile and it starts with Alphadjo Cisse. At first, it seemed he’d been wasted during the break, with Roberto Mancini not calling him up for the game against France.

According to recent reports, however, he was given the nod for the second game and got some valuable minutes on the field. As the Rossoneri have become familiar with, he took that chance with both hands, scoring a disallowed goal and winning a penalty in a defeat to Belgium.

He’s shining with confidence currently and long may it continue.

Sources indicate that then, Francesco Camarda is probably at the other end of the scale. He’s clearly not got the most confidence when representing the Diavolo, but returning to the youth level, he shone like he always has.

Against Sankhoun Diawara’s France side, he was excellent. In terms of his hold-up play, finishing and just general performance, he was almost perfect, if not perfect. With a goal to round it off too, he leaves the break with a much-needed confidence boost.

Unfortunately, we can’t say the same for Goncalo Ramos. After Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, this was a chance for him to take the star role and prove that he’s going to be the man to ensure things keep ticking.

Instead, he left the break leaving Portugal with more questions than answers, which is a familiar feeling.

He played just shy of 150 minutes during the break and mustered just one shot. It’s not like he provided an assist or any key passes either. In other words, it’s another blank for him and it’s clearly having an effect.

Without a goal in 661 minutes, it’s no shock why the Diavolo are so heavily pursuing a striker ahead of January.

Industry observers note that for France, it was a relatively quiet break for Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot. Neither performed especially well against Italy in a 3-1 loss at San Siro, though Rabiot was named as the captain for that game. Then, in the second game, Maignan was injured. However, it seems he’ll be fine for this weekend.

Not a lot to shout about for those two, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing either.

Sources indicate that for Luka Modric, his minutes were focused in the right areas. He played 14 minutes in a nothing game against England, but was then essential in a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic, which may help them qualify for the latter stages of the Nations League.

In a recent development, it was another strange international break for Ardon Jashari, too. He was given no minutes against Slovenia in a 0-0 draw, but then played the full 90 minutes against Scotland, where they won 4-0. He made 76 passes from 90 touches, so he had some involvement. However, he’s still a way away from being a dictator of the team, as it was hoped he’d be.

Davide Bartesaghi, Christian Comotto and Sankhoun Diawara were all given valuable minutes during the break. Finally, Pervis Estupinan played 36 minutes over the break. He returns without any injuries and that’s all there is to really say about his past fortnight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic made light work of St Mirren at the weekend as they ran out 4-1 winners on Saturday afternoon to maintain their lead at the Scottish Premiership.

Three goals in nine first-half minutes from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (33), Camilo Duran (40) and Luke McCowan (42) put the hosts on course for a comfortable victory, before captain Callum McGregor added to the scoreline in the second period (63). A Killian Phillips penalty (69) provided a consolation for the visitors.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It has been revealed that the win keeps Celtic four points clear at the top of the table after second-placed Rangers won 2-1 at Motherwell later in the evening kick-off. But what did their win over St Mirren tell us about Celtic’s hopes of winning a sixth successive league title come May?

Graham Falk was at Parkhead to cover proceedings. These are his three key takeaways from Celtic’s win vs St Mirren:.

It has been revealed that mika Baur’s injury looks like it may rule him out for up to 10 weeks and is clearly a major blow for Celtic. The young German has been one of their most impressive performers this season. With Benjamin Nygren also absent, Luke McCowan was handed his first start since September 20.

According to recent reports, forced to delete his social media account to escape personal abuse from sections of the online support just a few short weeks ago, it would have been hard to blame McCowan had he sunk into his shell when an audible groan greeted one of his early misplaced passes at Parkhead. But to McCowan’s credit, he did quite the opposite, and scored Celtic’s clinching third goal just before half-time.

According to recent reports, of course, one swallow doesn’t make a summer, but it’ll take a major weight off his shoulders, and could benefit Celtic with Baur out for a while. The ex-Dundee skipper will admit himself that he’s not been at the level expected this season. But, as proven by his 23 goal contributions across Celtic’s last two title-winning seasons, he’s shown previously that he can play an key role.

He’ll never be viewed as someone who will take Celtic to the next level, but he can take confidence from his performance and give O’Neill a valuable option as he awaits Nygren and Baur’s return to full fitness.

Sources indicate that in his previous stint as Celtic manager, the veteran boss loved to play with a front two. However, more out of necessity, he’s almost exclusively opted for a front three over the last 12 months. Previous managers Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers both moulded their side that way, and O’Neill has stuck with it. It’s had its doubters, though, with some calling for him to partner Kasper Hogh with Duran, rather than shifting the Colombian out on the wing to accommodate him.

But did the front three that started against St Mirren show a way forward for O’Neill? Starting Jota and Yang either side of Duran for the first time, the trio were a constant threat throughout for Celtic, who looked a more free-flowing outfit offensively than they have for several weeks.

“Yang is something else for us at the moment,” noted O’Neill post-match. “Duran is a top, top quality centre-forward, and Jota is still trying to get up to the speed of the game. But Yang is so strong, he made the first goal for us, and what he does for us defensively is just amazing when you consider he is a wide player.”.

It has been revealed that it was the main question before, during and after the game, in the stands and in the press room. The mystery surrounding Haissem Hassan. Where was he? One of Celtic’s significant summer signings, he was left out of the matchday squad for the second successive game, putting the rumours into overdrive.

Ahead of the game, O’Neill had quashed suggestions that the Egyptian was omitted from the squad for their last game because he was ‘unpopular’ with other members of his Celtic squad. However, his absence against St Mirren at the weekend was simply due to “rotation”. Hmm.

They didn’t miss him too much on the field, with Celtic rolling to a comfortable win over their Paisley counterparts. However, while no one can say Duran hasn’t repaid the £6million fee shelled out on him, the combined £20million spent on Hogh and Hassan is rightly being brought into question. We’re almost into December: one can’t get into the squad, and the other hasn’t scored a goal in over 1000 minutes. Surely O’Neill expected much more bang for his buck, even if he won’t admit it publicly.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.
  • Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 04:57.

Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.

Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.

Daniel Thioune guided Werder to safety last term after taking the helm in early February, though his sights are set much higher this time around with his team sat in a strong position upon the league's return.

Nine matches into the campaign, Die Werderaner are sixth in the Bundesliga table, where their tally of 15 points has them two clear of seventh-placed Elversberg and just three shy of RB Leipzig in fourth.

Securing European football of any variety would be a major accomplishment for Thioune, who is currently in his first top-flight role as manager, not to mention that the club last appeared on the continental stage back in the 2010-11 Champions League group stage.

However, Werder signed off for the international break with a 1-0 defeat at Stuttgart on November 7, their second loss in three matches after a 3-2 beating by Borussia Dortmund in the DFB-Pokal in late October.

In fairness to the Green-Whites, they fought back from 2-0 down against BVB thanks to a brace from Niclas Fullkrug, only to lose out to a stoppage-time free kick by Marcel Sabitzer.

Additionally, a 2-0 victory over Hoffenheim between those defeats saw the hosts maintain their unbeaten streak on home turf this season, where they will hope to record a fourth win in five outings on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Merlin Polzin's Hamburger endured a dire start to the season, conceding 12 goals without reply in their first three Bundesliga games before firing back with a run of three consecutive triumphs.

It would be fair to say that HSV's term has been defined by streaks so far, alternating between trios of defeats and wins across all competitions, and the club will be hoping to stabilise after the international break.

Polzin's side were held to a 1-1 draw by Croatia's Hajduk Split in a friendly on November 15, following up a 3-1 success against Borussia Monchengladbach that helped to distance the team from the relegation zone in the German top flight.

That victory has left Hamburger 11th in the Bundesliga table with 12 points to their name - a total that puts them level with Eintracht Frankfurt, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart up to eighth - as well as five points clear of 16th-placed Union Berlin.

Earning another win on Sunday would be keeping with HSV's pattern this term, but after seeing the visitors lose four of their five away league matches in 2026-27, fans would be forgiven for harbouring doubts.

Werder Bremen form (all competitions):.

Hamburger SV form (all competitions):.

Werder will be without strikers Keke Topp (ACL) and Salim Musah (thigh) once again as they recover from long-term injuries, though the doubts about Marco Grull's fitness after he missed training with a calf matter will be a major concern for the team.

If Grull is sidelined on Sunday, then expect to see Niclas Fullkrug supported up top by Eren Dinkci, Chuki and Justin Njinmah.

Jens Stage and Skelly Alvero are also unavailable due to respective thigh and calf injuries, while question marks remain about the readiness of fellow midfielder Senne Lynen, who has been ill over the past week, though Youri Regeer and Ludovit Reis should be on hand to form Thioune's double pivot.

Elsewhere, the versatile Mitchell Weiser is a doubt with a thigh problem and left-back Moussa N'Diaye is recovering from a groin injury, so Arthur and Olivier Deman look set to start at full-back.

As for Hamburger, they are missing centre-back Jordan Torunarigha, who has been dealing with a hip issue, but Mario Vuskovic is likely to return after getting over a minor back injury.

The visitors are lighter in midfield than ideal, with all three of Albert Sambi Lokonga (calf), Bilal Nadir (thigh) and Nicolai Remberg (ACL) sidelined, so Martin Adeline could join Miro Muheim in the centre of the park, while Albert Gronbaek operates in the number 10 role.

Centre-forward Yussuf Poulsen is also out with a calf injury, but Terem Moffi and Patson Daka will be ready to lead the line in a strike partnership on Sunday.

Werder Bremen possible starting lineup:.

Hein; Arthur, Friedl, Pieper, Deman; Regeer, Reis; Dinkci, Chuki, Njinmah; Fullkrug.

Hamburger SV possible starting lineup:.

Heuer; Capaldo, Omari, Bornauw; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Muheim, Moller Wolfe; Gronbaek; Moffi, Daka.

Werder have been exceptional on home turf this season, and they will be expecting to collect all three points once again, but the match is likely to be closer than otherwise if Grull remains sidelined.

By contrast, Hamburger have struggled on the road throughout 2026-27, and with four defeats in five away Bundesliga games so far, expect to see the visitors' overall pattern of results broken.

I watched Rangers down Motherwell and spotted Ibrox’s new leading man, injury blow plus eyebrow-raising stat

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rangers maintained their strong run of domestic form by defeating Motherwell 2-1 at Fir Park.

Recent findings suggest that emmanuel Fernandez had his headed opener for the away side cancelled out by a Jake Girdwood-Reich effort before Ryan Naderi’s deflected winner. It means Rangers are second and four points behind Premiership leaders Celtic with a game in hand while Motherwell sit 10th after their latest defeat.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

I was at the game played in bitterly cold North Lanarkshire conditions. Here are some of the things I spotted.

Recent findings suggest that whisper it in hushed tones... but this is the type of game that teams who go on to clinch silverware usually grind out. The expected goals tally of both sides show the tale of the tape, where not too dissimilar to Rangers’ 1-0 at Ibrox last time out, Derek McInnes’ side battered on the door without getting through.

Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was doing his best ‘you shall not pass’ Gandalf impression, but much like The Balrog dragging the grey wizard from Lord of the Rings into the abyss, eventually his resistance was broken. It was messy but Rangers cared not as they got their winner just before a minimal amount of stoppage time was added on. It’s a clash teams of the recent past in Govan coughed points up in and making it 13 unbeaten domestically will be of great satisfaction to boss McInnes.

Recent findings suggest that motherwell under Alfred Johansson have set their stall out as a side who want to dominate the ball but that hasn’t happened in either home game against Rangers or Celtic. Both sides of the Old Firm have come to Fir Park and been able to dictate play, Martin O’Neill’s side winning 2-0 last month, having controlled proceedings with well over 60% possession. This was much the same albeit the Fir Park defence stood valiantly until they were eventually overwhelmed, Rangers enjoying just under that 60% mark in terms of time on the ball.

Motherwell fans, and supporters of other provincial clubs, have been used to these types of games against Glasgow’s major two over the years. It’s a defensive stand that more often than not ends in defeat, but it’s more of a shock to the system for Motherwell, given what they have built over the last 18 months. Rangers’ winner was perhaps harsh with the effort put in but the amount of chances coughed up proved there could be little complaints over their visitors claiming all three points. Key playmaker Ibrahim Mentioned looked visibly emotional after being subbed in the first half with injury and that will be of major concern to boss Johansson, with much of his side’s good attacking play usually involving the Nigerian.

Since replacing an injured Lawrence Shankland last time out versus Motherwell, Ryan Naderi has been a man transformed. He bundled home the winner off defender Martin Moormann here to make it 11 goal contributions in as many games. Questions over quality were abundant last term upon his arrival from Hansa Rostock but he has been vital for McInnes this term.

Amid long-term blows to Shankland and Youssef Chermiti, Naderi has firmly made himself Rangers’ main man in attack. Any striker coming into the team would need to play alongside him as it’s hard to see how they function without him. It might be unconventional at times but Naderi’s pressing and knack of being in the right place at the right time is proving invaluable.

This clash between Motherwell and Rangers was the first time since Opta records began in season 2005/06 that there was not one Scottish player in the starting line-up of a top-flight match. As conversations continue over development of young talent in our country, it’s perhaps inevitable it became a talking point across analysis of the match.

Let’s get off our high horses for a minute though as the conversation with this particular game needs more nuance. Alex Lowry and Stephen O’Donnell are regular starters for Motherwell but both were unavailable, while club captain Paul McGinn is only recently back from long-term injury. James Penrice would likely have been a starter for Rangers had he been fully fit while Findlay Curtis did get on to make a key impact in the winner. Callum Hendry offered more bite to the home attack at the other end. All of that is not to say a lack of development Scottish talent isn’t an problem, it is, but perhaps this stat isn’t the platform to build that argument from.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The win came in Kevin Blackwell’s first game as permanent manager after his appointment earlier this week.

A goal in either half from Kai Jennings, Pemi Aderoju and a resolute back-line performance earned Crawley a deserved win.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It takes the Reds to within three points from safety, with as many games in hand against 22nd-placed Rochdale.

Reds made a fast start to the first half and took the lead in the fourth minute through Jennings, following Kellan Gordon’s cross from a darting run down the right wing.

Fleetwood, Arsenal’s conquerors and League Cup quarter-finalists, failed to clear their lines on the edge of the six-yard box and Jennings pounced on their indecision to smash home into the roof of the net.

Latest Reds centre back Ben Heneghan blocked a well-hit shot from range in the Cod Army’s first effort on goal in the ninth minute.

Vito Mannone calmy claimed Jake Batty’s left-wing cross to dispel Fleetwood as the away side got a foothold in the game and started to up the pressure, shortly before Reds nervily dealt with an Andy Cannon cross.

On the 15-minute mark Aderoju found himself through one-on-one but shot straight into the welcoming arms of Fleetwood keeper Jay Lynch.

Mannone was called upon to punch clear a couple of searching Fleetwood crosses into the box and lifted the pressure of his side in an open context.

Dylan Mogan nearly put the Reds 2-0 up on the half hour, he tricked his way past the Fleetwood right-back but curling shot from the edge of the box clipped the post and went out for a goal kick.

Just before the break Fleetwood’s Aaron Loupal-Bi got into a good position on the left after a one-two but his tame effort along the ground was collected by Mannone.

Reds flew out the traps to double their lead within a minute of the restart, Morgan stormed through Fleetwood’s midfield and slotted Aderoju in on-goal and the significant target man rifled a left-foot shot into the back of the net.

The visitors responded by almost pulling one back from a curling shot from the edge of the box and then hit the post moments afterwards.

Reds first chance of the second half fell to Aderoju who rose well but headed just wide from Gordon’s good right-side delivery.

Fleetwood gave themselves a lifeline thanks to substitute Will Davies’ firing a shot past Mannone from the middle of the penalty area to give the travelling fans behind the goal a reason to cheer.

Reds matched Fleetwood as the physicality grew as the half wore on and dug in to match their opponents.

Fleetwood substitute Lewis McCann stung the gloves of Mannone and produced a match-winning save from the big Italian who’s clean sheet was hard-earned.

Duke-McKenna had the chance to seal the points for the Reds at the end after chopping back onto his left foot down the right side, but his curled shot was parried away by Lynch.

Crawley are back at Broadfield in league action again this Tuesday (November 24) as they aim to climb out of the drop-zone in a tough test against high-flying Barnet.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.
  • Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.

Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.

As a result, UEFA have fined the FA and banned away fans from attending one UEFA match for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.

That said, the ban will only take effect if England supporters reoffend within the next two years.

It is a fortunate reprieve given the Three Lions' next away fixture is their Nations League quarter-final, the draw for which is on Friday.

Meanwhile, the FA have committed to identifying those involved and taking action - which could see football banning orders imposed.

In a statement to Daily Mail Sport, the FA said: 'We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.'.

England fans land FA in hot water over 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' chant during Spain victory.

Industry observers note that england supporters have notoriously sung the anti-Catholic and loyalist chant. In 2024, the Irish police urged travelling fans to 'respect local culture' before their Nations League match against the Republic of Ireland.

Fans were also filmed in Milan city centre on the eve of the clash against Italy in 2022 singing the same incendiary chant - just one year after their European Championship final defeat to the Italians.

Meanwhile, then England boss Roy Hodgson and the FA were forced to condemn supporters after the inflammatory chant was heard throughout England's 3-1 friendly victory over Scotland at Celtic Park in 2014. Around 5,000 fans travelled to the devoutly Catholic club.

The problem is not limited to international football. In August, Daily Mail Sport revealed that Chelsea wrote to supporters after a section of their fans were heard singing the sectarian chant away at Fulham on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was asked about racism in his pre-Spain press conference.

'I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on Earth and that's exactly how it works,' Tuchel mentioned.

'I expect emotional and of course supporting fans from Spain for their national team. That's what I expect, but I don't expect racism nowhere.

'I'm shocked if it happens, and it should happen nowhere, and I'm the first one to stand up for these kind of values.

'My trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: bring people together and not divide people.'.

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic has admitted that he was a fan of Sergio Conceicao, even if his management was rather totalitarian.

Sources indicate that it’s fair to say that Conceicao is a divisive figure within the Milan sphere. The Portuguese arrived and won the Supercoppa Italiana and there were glimpses of the Rossoneri becoming a team under him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, there were far too many incidents which turned most against him – including some members of the squad – and that gave him little hope of continuing. So, when he lost the Coppa Italia against Bologna, he was all but done, if he wasn’t before then.

He’s called it unfair since, but logically there was no way he could’ve continued.

Speaking to the Serbian podcast SS Calcio, Pavlovic admitted that he was fond of Conceicao, despite some of his strange methods, as MilanNews relays.

Industry observers note that “Conceicao banned Nutella, and since then they haven’t allowed it [he laughs]. He was… He’s a good guy, I like him, but he had Hitler-like methods. We go away for a match and at the hotel we split up; the players stay together, everyone else stays outside.

“Knee and elbow pads are mandatory in training, whether the temperatures are below zero or 35 degrees; they have to be there.

“Three days before a match, some players went to a concert until 11 p.m.… He had assistants, or spies if you like, who reported to him, and he made such a circus out of it that in the next match, none of those five or six players were allowed on the pitch.”.

Another anecdote about Conceiçao, when he had just been appointed coach of Milan….

“He was 40 minutes late to the first meeting; all the players and management were waiting for him, and he was in his office. He just wanted everyone to know who was in charge. He did it on purpose.”.

It’s certainly a strong comparison to make; that’s for sure….

Today's Premier League predictions include Arsenal's trip to Newcastle United, and a contest between Manchester City and Fulham.

Seeking to end a three-game losing run in the Premier League, Manchester City welcome Fulham to the Etihad Stadium for Saturday’s lunchtime kickoff.

These two teams last butted heads nine months ago when three first-half goals helped the Citizens claim a comfortable 3-0 home victory.

Maresca will demand a strong reaction from his Man City players following recent setbacks, and their exceptional historical record in this fixture firmly establishes them as the favourites to claim all three points.

While a porous Citizens backline offers encouragement to a Fulham outfit that has drawn a blank in seven of their last 12 Premier League games on the road, we expect the hosts' attacking firepower to comfortably outgun the Cottagers on this occasion.

These two teams served up a nine-goal thriller in the EFL Cup just a couple of months ago, with the West Londoners securing a 6-3 comeback victory in the third round.

Chelsea have not been the same prolific outfit without the presence of Joao Pedro up front, and they could find it difficult to break down a robust Leeds backline without a natural focal point.

Aston Villa's game management has become a growing concern, and Sunderland should fancy their chances of finding the net given that the hosts have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last six matches in all competitions.

While the Black Cats will be desperate to build on their victory over Chelsea as they bid to climb away from danger, the absence of both Xhaka and Brobbey is a real blow, and we expect Villa to ultimately navigate their way to a narrow triumph on home soil.

Separated by three places in the Premier League table, 12th-placed Tottenham Hotspur welcome Ipswich Town to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday seeking a return to winning ways on matchday 11.

Leeds United halted Spurs' three-match league winning streak before the hiatus, and the capital club now aim to begin a seemingly favourable run of fixtures with a positive result against the Tractor Boys.

Ipswich have scored four goals across their last two away matches, offering encouragement that their varied attacking threats can trouble a Tottenham side carrying several fitness concerns.

Nevertheless, the visitors' inability to keep opponents quiet on their travels should provide enough opportunities for Spurs to secure another home success.

> Click here to read our full preview for Tottenham vs. Ipswich, including team news and predicted lineups.

Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.

Frank's appointment should provide Palace with renewed purpose, but Mateta's suspension and doubts over Sarr and Strand Larsen leave the visitors short of attacking options.

Coventry have scored seven goals across their last three home matches and could exploit the Eagles' defensive uncertainty to spoil the Dane's first assignment.

Eyeing up a place in the top four of the Premier League, in-form Bournemouth welcome Nottingham Forest to the Vitality Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The spoils were shared in the last meeting between these two teams in May, with an opener from Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White cancelled out in the second half by Cherries attacker Marcus Tavernier to rescue a 1-1 draw.

Both Bournemouth and Forest enter this contest in buoyant mood as they look to build on positive results prior to the international break.

Although six of Forest's last seven Premier League away games have seen both teams score, we are backing the Cherries to frustrate an opponent they have historically enjoyed facing and secure three more points without reply to extend their impressive winning run to nine matches.

A modern Premier League rivalry will be renewed on Saturday evening, when champions Arsenal make the long trek north to battle Newcastle United following the international break.

The Gunners entered the hiatus on the back of a fifth straight win, edging out Hull City 1-0, while Matthias Jaissle's inconsistent troops settled for a 1-1 draw at Fulham.

While the break came at a better time for Newcastle than Arsenal, an increasingly familiar fate is set to befall the Magpies at St James' Park.

The champions' defensive might is showing no sign of wavering, nor is their ability to grind out victories in challenging circumstances, so we anticipate another 1-0 to the Arsenal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goals from Kai Jennings and Pemi Aderoju put the Reds in control in Blackwell’s first game in charge since his appointment until the end of the season on Thursday (November 19).

Will Davies’ late goal for the visitors made it a nervy finale.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But the hosts defended resolutely to earn only their second win in the league this campaign – and their first at home since March.

And Blackwell, while pleased to earn all three points, is keen to promptly build on the positive result.

He stated: “It's always great when you win, isn't it? And it's been a long time coming this season, so we will enjoy it but know that we've got a tough game against Barnet on Tuesday [November 24].

“It's just that process now of games coming and hopefully trying to improve the squad and improve the team, and hopefully we get some more results at home.”.

Despite the win, Crawley remain bottom of League Two but are unbeaten in their last three games.

Blackwell referenced the high stakes presently at play each time the Reds are in action.

Industry observers note that he said: “When you're down where we are, if it can go wrong, it will go wrong. So, we've got to be careful. We don't take risks in some areas. Make sure we fight our socks off. It's as simple as that.

It has been revealed that “We're in a dogfight. I want plenty of dogs fighting for us. And you saw today, everybody was fighting for the cause, and that's what I want. They've got to be proud to be a professional footballer, proud to be at Crawley Town, and proud to work for me.”.

Blackwell added: “I said to the boys as we went out, ‘this is Crawley Town, this is our home. I don't want anybody coming here thinking, ‘oh, we're playing Crawley, it’s nice and easy’.

It has been revealed that “I want them to go back thinking, ‘we've got to get on the bus and do a five-hour trip after being at Crawley’. That's what I want. And I think today, Fleetwood will get on the bus and think, ‘that was a tough one at Crawley today’.”.

As the Reds boss alluded to, his side are back in action at the Broadfield against second-placed Barnet on Tuesday night.

  • But his ousting has drawn an angry reaction from many on social media, with some saying it is a ‘disgraceful’ decision.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Macdonald has paid the price for a winless run that has seen Town slip to second from bottom of the division in their third season back at step four after promotion from the SCFL in 2024.

But his ousting has drawn an angry reaction from many on social media, with some saying it is a ‘disgraceful’ decision.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

A statement issued by the club a couple of hours after the first reports on X that the decision had been made mentioned: “Eastbourne Town F.C have today parted organization with First Team Manager Jude MacDonald and his coaching staff.

"The Committee would like to place on record their sincere thanks to Jude and his management team for their hard work over the last 4½ years, where, following their arrival, they quickly reshaped the remaining playing squad, and with some exciting new arrivals, just two years later launched an amazing mid-season recovery to storm up the SCFL Premier Division table to finish runners-up and then win the league play-off final.

“They then successfully kept the club in the Isthmian FL for successive seasons when largely up against many teams with much greater budgets and resources, a feat which we believe must be seen as a remarkable achievement in what is known by many to be a very tough division.

In a recent development, "The club wish them all the very best for the future and thank them once again for their service during their time at The Saffrons. No further statements will be made at this time.”.

Earlier in the day Town held Whitstable – third in the league – to a 0-0 draw at The Saffrons , a week after a 1-1 draw with Sheppey, who are also in the top half.

Recent findings suggest that at the end of the Whitstable game, the club’s X account noted: “A brilliant performance from The Town. A hard earned point and it could have been three after an excellent second half.”.

The news comes just a day after the club confirmed the return to the club of James Stone and James Waters.

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (467 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 21 Nov 2026 00:10.
  • Today's La Liga predictions include Real Madrid's clash with Celta Vigo, and the Seville derby between Sevilla and Real Betis.
  • Two teams that have enjoyed solid starts to their respective 2026-27 La Liga campaigns will lock horns on Saturday, with Alaves hosting Deportivo La Coruna.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 21 Nov 2026 00:10.

Today's La Liga predictions include Real Madrid's clash with Celta Vigo, and the Seville derby between Sevilla and Real Betis.

Two teams that have enjoyed solid starts to their respective 2026-27 La Liga campaigns will lock horns on Saturday, with Alaves hosting Deportivo La Coruna.

The visitors have been one of the surprise packages of the season thus far following their promotion from the second tier last term.

Only two points separates these two teams in the La Liga table, and we are expecting a close match on Saturday, with the points potentially being shared in a low-scoring draw.

> Click here to read our full preview for Alaves vs. Deportivo La Coruna, including team news and predicted lineups.

Rayo Vallecano and Valencia will both be looking to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume their respective La Liga campaigns in Madrid on Saturday.

Valencia's last match at this level ended in a 3-0 reverse to Real Madrid, while Rayo were beaten 1-0 by Real Sociedad in their final fixture ahead of the November international break.

Recent history points to a draw on Saturday, with the two teams sharing the spoils on a number of occasions of late; a close match could potentially finish 1-1.

> Click here to read our full preview for Rayo Vallecano vs. Valencia, including team news and predicted lineups.

The latest instalment of the Seville derby will take place at Estadio Ramon on Saturday evening, as Sevilla and Real Betis lock horns in La Liga.

A upcoming idea has emerged for AC Milan to strengthen their attack, and it is a player that incoming Head of Football Markus Krösche knows well.

According to recent reports, this morning’s edition of Tuttosport writes that the two dreams for January are Nicolò Tresoldi and Endrick, but a third option is starting to emerge at Milan. The player is equally effective in terms of goals, but perhaps less media-burdened than Gonçalo Ramos.

Industry observers note that the Portuguese striker has just three goals so far for Milan since joining for a club-record €73m fee, and his current drought is now over one month. This is why finding a viable alternative in the winter is key, but perhaps without spending another €60-70m on another forward.

It will be very hard to snatch Tresoldi from Club Brugge during the winter transfer window, as Arsenal and Atletico Madrid are also strongly interested in him. Meanwhile, Endrick’s departure from Real Madrid is at the moment being vetoed by Jose Mourinho. So, who could the Rossoneri turn to?

Milan could look towards the Bundesliga, more specifically Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic. He is a name highly regarded by Milan’s latest Head of Football – Markus Krösche – who has watched him up close for several years.

The Bosnian striker’s contract expires in 2028, and there’s presently no agreement to extend it. Therefore, his price tag – despite an  excellent start to the season – isn’t likely to skyrocket and could become affordable.

According to recent reports, he’s already scored nine goals across all competitions: five in nine appearances in the league, and four in four in the Champions League. That seems to provide enough evidence that the Bosnia international is ready for a top club.

Ermedin Demirovic has scored a hat-trick in the first 32 minutes of Stuttgart's game with Viking.

It's the fifth earliest in Champions League history:.

In recent weeks, the presence of Milan scouts at Stuttgart’s matches has not gone unnoticed. Demirovic has responded in his own way: with goals. Dzeko’s heir in the Bosnian national team can also play as a second striker and therefore, if necessary, partner Ramos.

In the past he has also been used as a winger in a three-man attack. This versatility is invaluable for a chameleon-like coach like Ruben Amorim, and it would allow Ermedin to be used in any type of situation.

Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 91 min read (18127 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~91 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and is often considered to be an adaptive behaviour driven by ecological or social pressures1,2.
  • Locusts provide a compelling model for studies of cannibalism because of its important role in collective dynamics5,6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and can profoundly influence individual fitness and population dynamics1,2. Although the ecological and social conditions that favour cannibalism have been well documented2, the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria, guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei. Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial–chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and is often considered to be an adaptive behaviour driven by ecological or social pressures1,2. However, its occurrence is highly context-dependent, and the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In humans, cannibalism largely disappeared with cultural evolution, partly owing to prion diseases3. Similarly, insects such as crickets rarely engage in cannibalism under normal conditions, but confinement or nutritional deprivation can trigger this behaviour4. These observations highlight the influence of environmental pressures on cannibalism, although its intrinsic regulatory mechanisms remain unclear.

Locusts provide a compelling model for studies of cannibalism because of its important role in collective dynamics5,6. In juvenile migratory bands, the threat of conspecific predation from behind promotes forward movement, reducing cannibalistic risk and contributing to group cohesion5,6. Cannibalism also provides nutritional benefits, allowing locusts to compensate for food deficiencies and potentially enhancing survival and movement capacity7,8. This behaviour is strongly influenced by density-dependent phase polyphenism. At low densities, solitarious locusts avoid conspecifics, whereas increased population density promotes gregarious behaviour and cannibalistic encounters5,7. Nutritional deficiencies further exacerbate cannibalism. Field studies of South American locusts (Schistocerca cancellata) have demonstrated that carbohydrate deprivation promotes cannibalism9, whereas laboratory studies on desert locusts (Schistocerca gregaria) have shown that protein-biased diets reduce movement and increase cannibalistic interactions7. Although these findings establish the ecological importance of cannibalism, its molecular and genetic regulation remains poorly understood.

Sources indicate that chemical cues regulate diverse locust behaviours, including aggregation10,11, oviposition12, mating13 and cannibalism14. Our previous work identified phenylacetonitrile (PAN) as a density-dependent anticannibalistic pheromone that activates specific olfactory receptors and reduces conspecific predation in crowded populations14. However, whether chemical cues actively induce cannibalism has remained unclear. Field and laboratory observations indicate that injured locusts are preferentially targeted by conspecifics15, suggesting that injury-induced chemical signals may attract individuals and promote cannibalistic behaviour.

Guaiacol, a volatile compound produced by gut microbiota during plant digestion, has been identified as an aggregation pheromone in desert locusts16. Here we show that injury-induced microbiota-derived guaiacol coordinates immune defence and cannibalism in migratory locusts (Locusta migratoria) and elucidate the underlying mechanisms, which span microbial biosynthesis, olfactory detection, immune regulation and behavioural responses. Together, our findings identify a microbial signalling mechanism linking immunity and cannibalism, revealing how host–microbe interactions mediate a trade-off between immune protection and vulnerability to conspecific predation.

Cannibalism in L. migratoria exhibits phase polyphenism, with solitarious nymphs typically avoiding conspecific predation, whereas gregarious nymphs are more prone to engage in cannibalism, particularly under conditions of crowding or food scarcity14. Preliminary observations indicated that injured individuals were rapidly surrounded and attacked by nearby conspecifics (Fig. 1a), suggesting that injury itself serves as a cue that increases susceptibility to conspecific predation. To test this hypothesis, we conducted dual-choice assays with gregarious fourth- and fifth-instar nymphs, the developmental stages at which cannibalism is most prevalent14. As injury can alter locomotor performance and therefore influence predator choice independently of injury-derived signals, we controlled for this potentially confounding factor by immobilizing both prey individuals. This experimental design enabled us to specifically evaluate the contribution of injury-associated cues to predator preference. In each assay, pairs of immobilized intact and injured fourth-instar nymphs were presented at opposite ends of a chamber containing ten starved fifth-instar predators (Fig. 1b). Injuries were induced either mechanically or by previous conspecific bites. Across all assays, predators consistently exhibited a marked predation preference for injured over intact prey, indicating a significant role of injury in heightening vulnerability to conspecific predation (Fig. 1c).

Recent findings suggest that a, Representative image of fifth-instar gregarious nymphs attacking an injured fourth-instar gregarious nymph. b, Schematic of the dual-choice predation assay. Ten starved fifth-instar gregarious nymphs were presented with one intact and one injured fourth-instar nymph immobilized at opposite ends of the arena. c–f, Predation preferences of intact (c; n = 15; group 1, P = 0.009; group 2, P = 0.012), ommatidectomized (d; n = 15; group 1, P = 0.001; group 2, P = 0.006), antennectomized (e; n = 15) and LmOrco−/− (f; n = 14) nymphs. Three prey pairings were tested: group 1, intact versus bitten; group 2, intact versus mechanically injured; group 3, mechanically injured versus bitten. g, Schematic of the dual-choice olfactometer assay testing volatiles from intact and injured fourth-instar nymphs. h,i, Olfactory preference of wild-type (h; n = 19; group 1, P = 0.010; group 2, P < 0.001) and LmOrco−/− (i; n = 15) nymphs for the three pairings described above. Statistical analyses were performed using two-sided paired-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. ***P < 0.001; ** P < 0.01; * P < 0.05; NS, not significant.

In a recent development, to determine whether the type of injury influenced predation preference, we compared predator preferences between mechanically injured and bitten prey. No significant difference was observed (Fig. 1c), indicating that injury alone, regardless of its origin, is sufficient to induce preferential predation. To explore whether injury-induced vulnerability was consistent across developmental stages, we extended the assays to first- to fifth-instar nymphs as prey. In all stages tested, fifth-instar predators consistently preferred injured prey over their intact counterparts, irrespective of injury type (Extended Data Fig. 1a). These findings demonstrate that injury-driven cannibalism is a robust and consistent trait across the development of gregarious locusts.

Next, we investigated the sensory cues mediating injury-induced predation. To assess the roles of olfactory and visual inputs, we performed antennal ablation (disrupting primary olfactory input), knocked out olfactory coreceptor LmOrco (disrupting olfactory receptor function) (Extended Data Fig. 1b) or removed the compound eyes (disrupting visual input). Predators with removed compound eyes retained their preference for injured prey (Fig. 1d), suggesting that visual cues are not required to mediate this behaviour. By contrast, predators lacking antennae or LmOrco function indicated no preference for injured over intact prey (Fig. 1e,f). Notably, although antennectomized predators no longer exhibited a statistically significant preference, a weak residual bias towards injured prey remained (Fig. 1e). This observation was consistent with the anatomical organization of the locust olfactory system, in which the antennae constitute the principal but not the exclusive olfactory organs. Consequently, antennal removal might substantially reduce but not completely eliminate olfactory perception. By contrast, disruption of LmOrco, which broadly impairs odorant receptor function, resulted in a complete loss of discriminatory behaviour (Fig. 1f). Together, these findings identify LmOrco-dependent olfaction as the primary sensory modality mediating injury-induced cannibalistic predation.

Finally, we assessed whether volatile chemical cues contributed to the observed predation bias. Headspace volatiles from both injured and intact nymphs were collected and presented in a dual-choice olfactometer (Fig. 1g). Starved fifth-instar predators strongly preferred the zone containing volatiles from injured individuals over the zone containing volatiles from intact prey (Fig. 1h). No significant difference in preference was observed between volatiles from mechanically versus bitten prey (Fig. 1h), indicating that injury-induced volatile release enhances predator attraction, thereby increasing the susceptibility of injured individuals to cannibalism. By contrast, LmOrco−/− predators indicated no preference for the zone containing volatiles from injured individuals (Fig. 1i), indicating that LmOrco-dependent olfaction mediated the predation preference.

It has been revealed that to investigate the chemical signals underlying injury-induced cannibalism in L. migratoria, we analysed the headspace volatiles emitted by intact, mechanically injured and bitten locust nymphs (Fig. 2a). Among the compounds detected, guaiacol emerged as the dominant injury-affected odorant (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Table 1), with emission levels approximately ten-fold higher in injured nymphs compared with intact controls and gregarious adults (Fig. 2b,c and Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). This increase in guaiacol release was consistent across all developmental instars (first to fifth) (Extended Data Fig. 2c), suggesting that an increase in guaiacol production is a consistent physiological response to injury in gregarious nymphs. By contrast, other compounds—including PAN, which has previously been linked to suppression of cannibalism14—demonstrated no significant changes across injury conditions (Fig. 2b,c and Extended Data Fig. 2d), indicating that guaiacol is a key injury cue.
